methodology_note: Regenerated after the 2026-09-17 batch-inference-collapse fix (see train_ppo_blended_report.json): the champion was retrained on a BLEND of the offline CMAPSS run-to-failure corpus (supervisor_encoded_dataset.csv, 200 engines -- the only source of genuine failure examples) and the real merged live-regime corpus (supervisor_integrated_input.csv, 259 engines, after fixing impute_missing_values' global-median-fill bug in supervisor_cleaner.py). The 28 test engines below are the genuine run-to-failure held-out engines (offline slice) -- never used for training or checkpoint selection -- because the live-regime engines contain zero true failures (0/259 end with predicted_rul <= 2.0) and so cannot support a meaningful failure-prevention comparison. See policy_evaluation_report_live_slice.json for that slice's (trivial, no-failure) numbers.
interpretation: Champion now matches rule_cascade_baseline exactly on safety (0 catastrophic failures, identical 12.0h mean downtime, both 100% successful_scheduled_maintenance) while costing 84.2% less per engine ($500 vs $3,159). The saving comes from timing: rule_cascade engages monitor_closely/schedule_inspection as soon as its thresholds are crossed and accumulates their per-step cost for many cycles before finally escalating, while the champion waits (continue_operation is free) and intervenes at the same safe moment rule_cascade eventually reaches -- same outcome, materially cheaper. This was NOT true of the pre-fix champion (see champion_model_manifest.json history / ppo_pre_liveregime_backup.joblib): it had 1 catastrophic failure on this same test set, i.e. it was WORSE than rule_cascade on safety, not just cost.
